Consider the circle of radius $3$ centered at $(3,-2)$, as shown above. Which of the following sets of parametric equations, defined for $\theta \in [0,2\pi ),$  traverse the circle once in the counterclockwise direction starting at the point $A(6,-2)?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The parametric equations of a circle of radius $r$ centered at the point $(a,b)$ are

$$
x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +a,\,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +b,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$

Under this parametrization, the circle is traversed once in the counterclockwise direction, starting from $(r+a,b).$

In our case, we have a circle of radius $3$ centered at the point $(3,-2).$ Therefore, the parametric equations of the circle are

$$
x=3\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +3,\,y=3\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta -2,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$
